axis: How a round's selection is made, bound to its one-time commitments and tied to the puzzle signature.

architectures.name: Rolled subsets with separate commitments
architectures.mechanism: The construction of the Binohash paper. Pinning is four signature-size puzzles under keys with disjoint sighash targets, after a hardcoded SIGHASH_SINGLE signature that forces the SIGHASH_SINGLE bug (Appendix A). Each round pushes its own pool of n nine-byte signatures and, separately, n HASH160 commitments. The unlocking script supplies t indexes; for each, the script rolls the index up, clamps it, rolls out the commitment at that rank, checks a revealed preimage against it, and rolls out the signature at the same rank. The t selected signatures and the size-checked puzzle signature are verified by one (t+1)-of-(t+1) OP_CHECKMULTISIG whose FindAndDelete removes the selection from the scriptCode (Appendix B).
architectures.distinguishing: Signatures and commitments are two separate tables on the stack, a selection is an index walked through OP_ROLL once per table, and every round has a pool, a commitment table and a multisig of its own. The cost per selected element is fixed stack choreography; the cost per pool element is a signature push plus a commitment push.
references: R. Linus, Binohash: Transaction Introspection Without Softforks (2026), sections 3 to 6 and appendices A and B
L. Reyzin and N. Reyzin, Better than BiBa: Short One-Time Signatures with Fast Signing and Verifying, ACISP 2002
